original.statement: The citadel_server_root_cert_expiry_timestamp, citadel_server_root_cert_expiry_seconds, citadel_server_cert_chain_expiry_timestamp, and citadel_server_cert_chain_expiry_seconds metrics now update when new certificates are loaded.

corrected.statement: The citadel_server_root_cert_expiry_timestamp, citadel_server_root_cert_expiry_seconds, citadel_server_cert_chain_expiry_timestamp and citadel_server_cert_chain_expiry_seconds metrics now update when new certificates are loaded, instead of keeping stale values.

decision.reason: [ev-40e9ce81a63d] describes a bug fix: four emitted metrics (citadel_server_root_cert_expiry_timestamp/_seconds and citadel_server_cert_chain_expiry_timestamp/_seconds) now update when new certificates are loaded. That is a runtime behaviour change, not a change to a configuration key, so a config-key "metrics" subject is not supported. Nothing in the evidence names a config file or key called "metrics". behavior-changed is the right change type. Since no family covers metrics, the closest fit is a free-form runtime-behaviour subject named from the evidence's own key words. This mapping is approximate, so confidence is low.
